newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SARFU PLAYS DOWN MONEY ROW REPORT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SARFU PLAYS DOWN MONEY ROW REPORT.

text.p: South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) chief executive Rian Oberholzer on Monday dismissed newspaper reports of an impending player revolt over payment for the Springbok tour of Argentina, France and Wales.
"This story is devoid of truth," he said, referring to a story in Beeld that some Springbok players were demanding a 75 percent pay increase to tour.

"Players will always try and squeeze you for more money, but to say that they are about to revolt and strike is nonsense. We will meet with the player representatives later today but we will keep the results confidential."
According to Oberholzer payment for the tour is based on match appearances.
"If a player only plays midweek matches the least he will earn is 50,000 rand - I don't think that's bad, and obviously the test players will earn considerably more."
The newspaper report said leading players were seeking an additional 1,500 rand a day on top of a basic rate of 100,000 rand, effectively a 75 percent increase.
